diagnostic_evidence.quote: reveal favourable second-order convergence of our method whenever the exponential L{\'e}vy process has finite-variation.

issues.failure_explanation: In two dimensions, the leading quadratic f(z) is not generally proportional to ||z||^2, so f(z)/||z||^2 retains angular dependence at zero. There are finite-variation counterexamples even with densities smooth away from zero. Take 0<A<1, h_j=2^(-j!), and ell(z)=sum_j h_j^(-A-2)b(z/h_j), with a smooth positive bump b supported in (2.1,2.2)×(2.7,2.8). At mesh h_j that bump lies in a cell centered at (2.5h_j,2.5h_j). For the leading quadratic z1^2, the center ratio z1^2/||z||_2^2 is 1/2, whereas it is below 0.4 on the bump. This creates an error of order h_j^(2-A); contributions from other scales can be made negligible. The claimed second order therefore fails.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $G$ is a Tempered Stable subordinator

issues.failure_explanation: The construction never requires G to be independent of B, although the density formula used by the proof requires independent subordination. A concrete one-dimensional counterexample takes B=W and G(t) as the first time W(s)+a s reaches t. Then G is an inverse-Gaussian subordinator with alpha=1/2, delta=1/sqrt(2pi), and lambda=a^2/2, but L(t)=W(G(t))=t-aG(t). Its negative-jump density decays with exponential rate a/2, whereas the proposition's formula with eta=0 and rho=1 gives B_ell=a. Thus the asserted tail bound fails for a construction permitted as written.
